title: Smurfit Westrock France wins prestigious Choose France award
summary: Smurfit Westrock has been awarded the prestigious Choose France 2026 prize in the Territories & Talent category, recognising the company's continued investment in France, commitment to local communities and focus on developing employee skills and capabilities.
body_markdown:
***Success follows previous announcement of significant investment in the country***


Smurfit Westrock has been awarded the prestigious Choose France 2026 prize in the Territories & Talent category, recognising the company's continued investment in France, commitment to local communities and focus on developing employee skills and capabilities.


Presented as part of the annual États de la France event in Paris, the award recognizes international companies that have chosen France as a location for long-term growth and have successfully delivered on investment commitments announced through the French Government's Choose France programme.


The award was granted by a distinguished jury led by Pascal Cagni, President of Business France and Ambassador for International Investment, and acknowledges Smurfit Westrock's contribution to economic development, skilled employment and talent development in France.


In his acceptance speech, Andrew Coffey, CEO of Smurfit Westrock France, said: "This award is a tribute to our 6,000 colleagues across France whose expertise, passion and commitment enable us to deliver innovative, sustainable[paper-based packaging](https://www.smurfitwestrock.com/products/packaging) solutions to more than 7,000 customers every day.


“Their ability to combine innovation, operational excellence and close customer partnership is what makes us the leader in the French paper-based packaging market, and I am proud to accept this recognition on their behalf."


The Choose France awards celebrate international companies whose investments contribute to France's economic development and competitiveness.


The recognition follows Smurfit Westrock's announcement in June that it will invest €600 million across its operations in France, reinforcing its long-term commitment to French manufacturing, innovation, and sustainability.
